question: Texas claim counts jumped in May 2025. What happened?

sql:
WITH source AS (
    SELECT c.*, p.channel, p.metro,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) AS paid_to_date,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) + c.reserve_amount AS incurred,
           c.close_date - c.report_date AS days_to_close
    FROM claims c
    JOIN policies p USING (policy_id)
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY claim_id
    ) pay USING (claim_id)
)
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', loss_date) AS DATE) AS period, region, count(*) AS value
FROM source
WHERE loss_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND loss_date <= DATE '2025-09-30'
  AND region IN ('Texas')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL

report.interpretation: Texas region claim counts (agreed claim_count metric) by loss-date month, Jan–Sep 2025. I looked at why May 2025 jumped. Months that far back are essentially complete.
report.answer: The jump is real. Texas had 100 claims with May 2025 loss dates, against 64 in April and 68 in June. The cause was the Houston hailstorm on 20–21 May 2025 (weather event WX-001, rated moderate). It produced 26 auto hail claims on Houston policies with loss dates 20–23 May, and 25 of those 26 fall on 20–21 May. Without those 26 claims, May would have been 74, in line with the Jan–Jun range of 58–74. Policies in force were flat (about 9,350), so growth in the book doesn't explain it. The data has no duplicates or other quality problem that would explain the jump. It was a one-off event, and June went back to 68.
report.answer_sql: select cast(date_trunc('month', loss_date) as date) as loss_month, count(*) as claims, count(*) filter (where not (cause='hail' and p.metro='Houston' and loss_date between '2025-05-20' and '2025-05-23')) as ex_houston_hail from claims c join policies p using(policy_id) where c.region='Texas' and loss_date between '2025-01-01' and '2025-09-30' group by 1 order by 1

findings.claim: May 2025 Texas claims were 100 against 64 in April. 26 of them are Houston auto hail claims from 20–23 May, matching the Houston hailstorm on 20–21 May. Excluding them leaves 74.

hypotheses.evidence: WX-001 Houston hailstorm 20–21 May 2025. 25 of the 26 Houston hail claims have loss dates on those two days.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Growth in exposure or change in business mix
hypotheses.evidence: Texas policies in force were flat at about 9,330–9,385 from March to July 2025. The excess is concentrated in one cause and one metro.
The claims quality check found no duplicate rows. May 2025 is more than a year old, so late reporting isn't a factor.
Excluding the storm claims, May (74) is within the Jan–Jun range of 58–74. The spike is not noise.
